verdict.rationale: LangGraph's interrupt() mechanism explicitly pauses graph execution at specific points (e.g., before a sensitive tool call) and waits for external input before resuming via Command, and this is documented as a core human-in-the-loop pattern backed by checkpointer persistence; GitHub docs also tout 'human-in-the-loop' as a named feature for inspecting/modifying agent state during execution. Missing for 10: no explicit first-party example scoped precisely to 'approve before tool call' (vs generic interrupt points) and no independent/hands-on case study confirming this exact pattern in production.
